title: Current work: cartoons, big bands, Ellington alumni conference
summary: He describes his varied week, cartoon music, and an Ellington conference with Buster Cooper and John Lamb.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Whoa. He came around. Yeah. Well your weekly — a week for you, I can imagine every day is like a little different. Right.

It’s totally different, totally different. Like I book my own band, so when I have time to do that I spend as much as I can. Then I’ll have — I mean this Tuesday a friend of mine does a cartoon for kids called “The Backyardigans,” you ever hear of this?

It’s on Nickelodeon. I used to do another one called “Rocko’s Modern Life.” And I love playing that, cartoons. So this guy, so we’ll be there probably a good part of the day on Tuesday. Tuesday night I have a rehearsal for a big band for the one I was telling you about at this Quaker School and we’re going to do a concert for them on Thursday afternoon. And it’s just more stuff coming up. I mean you know I’m going to England. Oh, the band is going for about three days to a jazz festival. Then I’m going over as a guest at a Duke Ellington Conference in England. You know there aren’t many alumni © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
left, but Buster Cooper, the great trombone player in the sixties, he and I and this great bass player from then, John Lamb. They had a great—
You say hi for us. I’ve interviewed those guys.

Because we did something similar to this in California about four years ago. They had probably all the alumni left that they could find except for Clark couldn’t make it. And you remember Uhura from Star Trek? Do you know she sang with Duke?
Yeah. They couldn’t find her somehow. And we did performances which was great, and then we all did the history stuff.
